1. I will utterly consume and cut off
 - The name Tsephanyahu means "Yahweh hides."
<습1:1> 아몬의 아들 유다 왕 요시아의 시대에 스바냐에게 임한 여호와:
<Zeph 1:1> The word of the LORD which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah (son's grandson), the son of Hizkiah (grandson's grandson), in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.
 - Zephaniah was of royal descent, and right after introducing the author, what's the very first thing he says? I'll utterly consume and cut off everything. He's saying, I'll kill them all. In the passage we're reading now, let's underline the words "consume" and "cut off."
<습1:2~7> 여호와께서 이르시되 내가 땅 위에서 모든 것을 멸절하리라: <Zeph 1:2~7> I will utterly consume all things from off the land, saith the LORD. I will consume man and beast; I will consume the fowls of the heaven, and the fishes of the sea, and the stumblingblocks with the wicked; and I will cut off man from off the land, saith the LORD. I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with the priests;
또 지붕에서 하늘의 뭇 별에게 경배하는 자들과 경배하며 여호와께 맹세하면: And them that worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and them that worship and that swear by the LORD, and that swear by Malcham; And them that are turned back from the LORD; and those that have not sought the LORD, nor enquired for him. Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD: for the day of the LORD is at hand: for the LORD hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests.
지금 하나님께서 진멸하고 멸절하겠다는 사람들이 어떤 사람들이예요? 여기: So who are the people God says He will utterly consume and cut off? Here, 'Chemarims' means priests who serve foreign gods. The wicked, the remnant of Baal, the Chemarims, those who worship the stars of heaven, those who swear by the LORD and also swear by Malcham (Milcom, a foreign god also called Molech, a vicious one who had little children burned as offerings), those who turn away from the LORD and don't follow Him, and even those who don't seek the LORD or ask for Him.
<습2:3> 여호와의 규례를 지키는 세상의 모든 겸손한 자들아 너희는 여:
<Zeph 2:3> Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD'S anger.
 - Keeping the LORD's ordinances is what humility is. Usually, pretending to be humble and bowing and scraping is hypocrisy, fake goodness. He's saying He hides the people who seek righteousness and humility. He doesn't hide just anybody.
 - God hides people like that, but how does He hide them?  When a wild beast like a lion or a tiger is mauling people to death left and right, where's the safest place?  The tiger's den.
바벨론이라는 호랑이를 보내서 온 천지를 물어 죽이고 다닐 때 하나님께서:
When He sent the tiger called Babylon to go around mauling the whole world to death, God picked them up and moved them to Babylon. That is how God hides them.
 - From chapter 2 verse 4 on, it says that all the nations will be destroyed.
3. God, who looks at those He has hidden and can't contain His joy.
습3:17 너의 하나님 여호와가 너의 가운데 계시니 그는 구원을 베푸실:
Zeph 3:17 The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
 - This isn't a word spoken to us; it's spoken to the people who went into the Babylonian Exile and are coming back. Because of the people who went to Babylon, came to their senses, and returned, He can't contain His joy and loves them quietly. I told you, "to whom" is what matters, right?
